input.quote: the results of all such development efforts set forth in this Section 13, including all intellectual property rights in any software interface coding or programs created solely by Corio during the term of this Agreement to enable the Software to operated within the Corio Servers' hosted environment ("DEVELOPMENTS"), shall be owned by Corio, unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights, including
input.rationale: Section 13.5 starts from the right place (Developments created solely by Corio are owned by Corio, and Commerce One assigns any claim it may have), but the "unless supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One" carve-out flips ownership of work product we create to the Vendor, with no licence back to us. That is an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor and fails both the preferred and fallback positions on a material term. The redline deletes only the carve-out so Corio owns its Developments while Commerce One's pre-existing materials and Software ownership (Section 2.8) are untouched; if ongoing support is the concern, a support licence to Commerce One is the sensible fallback. Noted but not separately flagged: the final sentence of 13.5 leaves ownership of enhancements to the Software itself to future negotiation, and the Agreement contains no Customer Data ownership sentence (there is no Customer Data concept in this hosting licence).

proposal.summary: Delete the carve-out that transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where Commerce One supports them.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13.5 gives Commerce One ownership of interface coding created solely by Corio whenever Commerce One supports it on an ongoing basis, with no licence back to us; our playbook requires that we own the work product we create and fund, so we have deleted that carve-out. If ongoing support is the concern, we can instead grant Commerce One a licence to use such Developments for support purposes.
